name: Ascending Aorta Anomaly

criteria.description: Echocardiographic or imaging evidence of abnormal dilation or morphology of the ascending aorta
Histopathological or imaging evidence of abnormal aortic wall structure or thickening
Presence of associated congenital cardiac anomalies such as bicuspid aortic valve or aortic coarctation
Positive family history of ascending aorta anomalies or related connective tissue disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging-confirmed abnormal ascending aorta morphology or dilation plus at least one additional major or minor criterion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multimodal imaging and exclusion of acquired causes of aortic dilation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ascending aortic dilation detected on imaging

common.symptomName: Exertional dyspnea due to aortic valve insufficiency
searchTerms: exercise-related breathing difficulty from aortic valve

common.symptomName: Chest discomfort related to aortic root dilation
searchTerms: pain linked to aortic root expansion

common.symptomName: Systolic murmur from aortic valve abnormalities
searchTerms: abnormal heart sounds from valve issues

occasional.symptomName: Syncope related to compromised aortic flow
searchTerms: fainting due to poor aortic blood flow
passing out from blocked aortic flow

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
searchTerms: voice changes due to nerve pressure

occasional.symptomName: Cough caused by tracheal irritation from aortic enlargement
searchTerms: cough from enlarged aorta pressing trachea

rare.symptomName: Aortic dissection presenting with sudden severe chest pain
searchTerms: sudden severe chest pain from aortic tear
aortic dissection causing sharp chest pain
tearing chest pain due to aortic rupture

rare.symptomName: Heart failure symptoms due to progressive aortic insufficiency
searchTerms: heart failure symptoms from valve leak
fluid buildup and fatigue from aortic insufficiency

rare.symptomName: Stroke secondary to embolism from aortic pathology
searchTerms: stroke caused by blood clots from aorta
neurological deficits due to aortic embolism

laboratory: Genetic testing for connective tissue disorders if indicated
imaging: Echocardiography showing ascending aortic dilation or aneurysm
CT angiography or MRI confirming aortic morphology and dimensions
Chest X-ray may show widened mediastinum
genetic: Mutations in genes related to connective tissue disorders (e.g., FBN1, TGFBR1/2) in some cases
other: Histopathology may reveal cystic medial necrosis or elastic fiber fragmentation

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic connective tissue manifestations including skeletal and ocular abnormalities
Congenital valve morphology with two cusps instead of three
Associated with ascending aortic dilation but distinct valve pathology
Often presents with aortic stenosis or insufficiency

redFlags: Sudden onset severe chest or back pain suggestive of aortic dissection
Rapidly increasing ascending aortic diameter on serial imaging
Signs of heart failure or syncope in a patient with known aortic anomaly
